historical_record.description: Recorded in the city's survey of the Van Ness Avenue automobile corridor as built for use as an auto showroom. Dated 1908–1909. Designed by Frederick H. Meyer, and first numbered 583 Golden Gate Avenue — it stood at the corner of the city's first auto row, and in 1913 it held the Standard Motor Car Company. It is the one early Golden Gate Avenue auto showroom still standing with good integrity, its brick walls and cornice essentially unchanged. The first cars sold here were Ford and Velie — the oldest auto showroom in the city.
Recorded in the city's survey of the Van Ness Avenue automobile corridor as an early auto showroom, selling Lozier among other brands; altered.
Evaluated in the city's survey of the Van Ness Avenue automobile corridor and given California Register status code 3CS — individually eligible for the California Register, under Criteria 1 and 2.
Identified in the city's survey of the Van Ness Avenue automobile corridor but not formally evaluated on a state historic resource form.
